newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fazio confirms Rome wants to put lira back in ERM.
newsitem.headline: Fazio confirms Rome wants to put lira back in ERM.

text.p: Antonio Fazio, Governor of the Bank of Italy, confirmed on Friday that the Rome government had asked for the Italian lira to be readmitted to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
The lira was forced out of the close-knit exchange rate system in 1992.
Earlier on Friday, Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy wanted to take the currency back into the system by the end of the year.
Responding to a question at the European Banking Congress in Frankfurt, Fazio said "Our government has asked for the lira to re-enter the ERM."

Membership of Europe's exchange rate mechanism for at least two years before the start of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) is one of the economic conditions laid down for participation in a single European currency.

European countries that want to meld their currencies into the planned euro from the start in 1999 are scrambling to meet economic targets in 1997 on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budget deficits and public debt.

Fazio said Italy was making every effort to be ready for monetary union by the planned 1999 starting date. "My country is working very hard to be ready. We will be ready in a couple of years," he said.
